samples.summary: Canonical Docs design doc contradicts the shipped behavior; the change documents the reversal only in the CLI doc
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md` §Error Handling still states: line 414 `| Image fetch fails | Match DOCX behavior — throw (consistent across formats) |` and line 416 `| Unsupported image format | Convert to PNG via Canvas; if conversion fails, throw |`. This diff changes `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts` (`collectAndEmbedImages` now wraps fetch+decode+embed in a try/catch and reports through `onImageError`) and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts` (failed entries recorded with empty `rId`, run omitted), so both rows are now false. The new behavior is written up only in `docs/design/cli.md` §10 (lines ~1198-1210), i.e. a Docs-package architecture change is filed in the CLI's doc rather than folded into the canonical subsystem doc, which `docs/design/README.md` ('Obsolete docs' / filing-by-validity) and CONTRIBUTING require. `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md` (lines 439-440, the `imageFetcher` contract) is likewise untouched.

samples.summary: CLI-scoped fix silently changes browser export behavior in the shared @wafflebase/docs package, beyond the issue's acceptance criteria
samples.evidence: The todo (#655) scopes the image work to the CLI fetcher: 'An image `src` cannot aim an export at the local network…'. Nothing in it asks for a change to `@wafflebase/docs`. But `collectAndEmbedImages` and `DocxExporter.collectImages` are shared with the frontend export path (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts` passes `docsImageFetcher`), so browser PDF/DOCX exports now drop failing images with only a `console.warn` — no user-visible signal — where they previously failed loudly. The change's own doc admits this (`docs/design/cli.md` ~1204-1210: 'the *browser* PDF/DOCX exporters inherit the same swallow… surfacing dropped images in the browser export UI is follow-up work'), and the `catch` spans decode/embed as well as fetch, so the SSRF-refusal rationale does not cover all of what it now swallows. Either the swallow should be scoped to the fetch (or opt-in for CLI callers) or the product decision should be recorded in the Docs design docs and the browser UI wired.
searchedFor: grep frontend callers of docsImageFetcher / export-utils.ts

samples.summary: The doc that owns @wafflebase/core's contents still enumerates /url as isSafeUrl only, after seg() was added to that subpath
samples.evidence: `docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:131` reads `url/index.ts → @wafflebase/core/url (SAFE_PROTOCOLS, isSafeUrl) [shipped]` and line 184 describes `./url` as 'safe-protocol hyperlink gating'. This change adds `seg()` — a second, security-relevant primitive consumed by two clients — to that subpath (`packages/core/src/url/index.ts`) without updating the doc that catalogues what core exposes. cli.md and frontend.md were updated; the core doc was not.

samples.summary: assertNoDotSegments re-implements seg()'s dot-segment refusal, a second copy of the rule the change argues must have only one
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` and `packages/core/src/url/index.ts` justify hoisting `seg()` on the grounds that 'two copies of a security rule drift'. `printDryRun` then hand-rolls the same refusal locally (`assertNoDotSegments`, including a duplicate of the error string `Invalid path segment: "…"`), rather than exporting the predicate from `@wafflebase/core/url` next to `seg()`. If the refusal set ever grows (e.g. `%2e%2e` handling), the backstop is the copy that will be missed.

samples.summary: ~300 lines of URL/host-safety policy landed CLI-local while a sibling bounded-image-fetch guard already exists in the backend and the change's own argument puts URL-safety rules in core
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/miro/miro.service.ts` already owns the same class of guard for a document-controlled image URL: host gating (`isAllowedImageHost`, line 457), a declared+streamed byte cap (`readCapped`, line 479, and `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`), an image timeout (`IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS`, line 81) and `isTimeout` (line 668). The CLI now grows its own `isPrivateHost`/`isPrivateIpv6`/`unwrapIpv4`/`readCappedBlob`/`isTimeout`. The policies differ (allow-list vs private-address refusal) so this is not a literal duplicate, but the address/IPv6 classification is exactly the kind of URL-safety primitive the same diff argues belongs in `@wafflebase/core/url` alongside `isSafeUrl` and `seg()`; leaving it CLI-only means the backend cannot adopt it and the two will diverge.

samples.summary: §10 has grown into implementation narration duplicating the code comments verbatim
samples.evidence: The new §10 block (~180 lines) restates the image fetcher's implementation at line granularity — specific IPv4 ranges, 6to4/Teredo/NAT64 unwrapping, the four-address dial cap, the undici `host`-header limitation — largely word-for-word with the comments in `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts`. verdict.reason: The quoted evidence checks out and no counterexample exists. docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md:414 and :416 still state that a failed image fetch / failed format conversion throws, while packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:81-101 now catches per-image failures and reports them via onImageError (default console.warn at :17-20), and packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:441-455 records a failed entry with empty rId and omits the run (:211-213, :133-136). docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md:431-440 (image export flow + imageFetcher contract) is untouched and silent on the new drop semantics. A wide grep over all of docs/design/** for onImageError|collectAndEmbedImages|dropped|swallow|Skipping image finds the new behavior written up only in docs/design/cli.md:1198-1211 — which even notes that the browser PDF/DOCX exporters in @wafflebase/docs inherit the swallow. Per docs/design/README.md:45 (docs-pdf-export.md is the canonical Docs PDF-export doc) and README.md:168-179 (file by validity; fold notes into the canonical subsystem doc), a Docs-package behavior change documented only in the CLI doc while the canonical Docs doc asserts the opposite is a design-doc-discipline violation in this lens's lane (major).

finding.summary: CLI-scoped fix silently changes browser export behavior in the shared @wafflebase/docs package, beyond the issue's acceptance criteria
finding.evidence: The todo (#655) scopes the image work to the CLI fetcher: 'An image `src` cannot aim an export at the local network…'. Nothing in it asks for a change to `@wafflebase/docs`. But `collectAndEmbedImages` and `DocxExporter.collectImages` are shared with the frontend export path (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts` passes `docsImageFetcher`), so browser PDF/DOCX exports now drop failing images with only a `console.warn` — no user-visible signal — where they previously failed loudly. The change's own doc admits this (`docs/design/cli.md` ~1204-1210: 'the *browser* PDF/DOCX exporters inherit the same swallow… surfacing dropped images in the browser export UI is follow-up work'), and the `catch` spans decode/embed as well as fetch, so the SSRF-refusal rationale does not cover all of what it now swallows. Either the swallow should be scoped to the fetch (or opt-in for CLI callers) or the product decision should be recorded in the Docs design docs and the browser UI wired.
searchedFor: grep frontend callers of docsImageFetcher / export-utils.ts

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:51-104) wraps fetch, decode and embed in one try/catch and drops failing images via an `onImageError` reporter whose only wired implementation is the `console.warn` default (:17-20); `DocxExporter.collectImages` does the same (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:447-455). Both are on the browser export path (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pdf-actions.ts:31, docx-actions.ts:50, export-utils.ts:46 `docsImageFetcher`), and grep shows no caller injects a custom reporter, so browser exports silently drop images. The originating issue's image criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:78-84) is scoped to the CLI fetcher's SSRF refusal and asks for no `@wafflebase/docs` behavior change. The decision is recorded only in docs/design/cli.md:1198-1211 (which itself admits the browser swallow and the decode/embed over-broad catch as follow-up), while the canonical Docs subsystem doc still specifies the opposite behavior: docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md:414 "Image fetch fails — throw". That is an unrequested behavior change in a shared package plus a design-doc-discipline violation (product change documented in the wrong doc, canonical doc left contradicting the code) — major under this lens.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (3) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding cites no file, line, acceptance criterion, duplicated module, or design doc. Its text is verbatim the error string produced by the review harness itself when its API credential pool is exhausted: `poolExhaustedError` at .trusted/scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 builds exactly `${label}: every credential in the pool (${pool.size}) was retired — nothing left to fail over to` (label "review", pool.size 3), and the "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict:" prefix is the panel wrapper reporting the lens agent never returned a structured verdict. That behavior is intentional and unit-tested (.trusted/scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:302,321,341,354) and documented at ask.mjs:610-628. So no defect in the reviewed code is described — it is an infrastructure/credential-exhaustion abort of the reviewer process. It also raises nothing in the design-fit lane (spec conformance, reuse/duplication, scope, design-doc discipline). Ground: not-present, since the asserted defect has no locatable subject in this repository.
